questions.question: Find the average of first 20 multiples of 9.
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Sum of n natural numbers = n(n + 1)/2

The sum of the first 20 multiples of 9 

⇒ 9(1 + 2 + 3 +…+ 20)

⇒ 9 × 20 × 21/2

⇒ 1890

Average of first 20 multiples of 9

⇒ 1890/20

⇒ 94.5

**∴ The answer is 94.5.**

questions.question: Find the value of equation a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc. if a² + b² + c² = ab + bc + ca + 4 and a + b + c = 4.
questions.solution:
As we know, (a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc) = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² – ab – bc – ca)

Given, a² + b² + c² = ab + bc + ca + 4

⇒ a² + b² + c² – ab – bc – ca = 4

∴ (a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc) = 4 × 4 = 16

questions.question: What is the x – intercept of the linear equation 18x + 25y – 900 = 0?
questions.solution:
x – intercept is the point at which the line crosses the x – axis, i.e. y = 0

Putting y = 0 in the equation,

⇒ 18x + 25(0) – 900 = 0

⇒ 18x = 900

⇒ x = 900/18 = 50

∴ x – intercept is 50

questions.question: Two equal circles intersect each other at point A and B, whose centers are O and O’. OO’ = 24 mm and AB = 10 mm, then find the area (in sq. mm) of the circle.
questions.solution:
The given circles can be drawn as shown below

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/744d21680b2a3c4ecced031dd8da8e1fae33124a9199580eaeb7632340a9b9a9.png] 

Let P be the intersection point of AB and OO’

AP = AB/2 = 10/2 = 5 cm

OP = OO’/2 = 24/2 = 12 cm

Considering ∆AOP,

AO² = OP² + AP²

⇒ AO² = 144 + 25 = 169

⇒ Radius of circle = AO = √169 = 13 cm

∴ Area of circle = πr² = 3.14 × 13 × 13 = 530.66 cm²

questions.question: The length of the diameter of the circle is 10 cm and length of the chord drawn in a circle is 6 cm. Find the distance (in cm) of chord from the center.
questions.solution:
Let AB be the diameter of the circle with centre O and CD be the chord in the circle, as shown below

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3279e83b8413d8a9d7485bdd563ad539b0d2eee0e56ded6e11ef9c269d8cac53.png] 

OC = OD = OA = OB = radius of circle = 10/2 = 5 cm

OE = Distance between chords and the centre of the circle

Perpendicular drawn from the center of the circle bisects the chord; radius always bisects the chord if perpendicular.

CE = CD/2 = 6/2 = 3 cm

Considering ∆OCE,

OE² = OC² – CE²

⇒ OE² = 25 – 9 = 16

∴ Distance between chord and centre = OE = √16 = 4 cm

X, Y and Z are partners in a company. In one year X receives 1/4 part of profit, Y receives 1/5 part of profit and Z receives Rs. 22000. How much amount (in Rs.) will X get as profit?
questions.solution:
Part of profit received by Z = 1 – (1/4 + 1/5) = 1 – 9/20 = 11/20

⇒ 11/20 of Total profit = 22000

⇒ Total profit = 22000 × 20/11 = Rs. 40000

∴ Profit received by X = 1/4 × 40000 = Rs. 10000

questions.question: P and Q started a business by investing Rs. 50000 and Rs. 40000 respectively. After 4 months, P withdraws Rs. 20000 while Q invests Rs. 70000 more after 6 months of starting the business. At the end of the year P’s share in the profit is Rs. 11000. What will be the total profit (in Rs.) at the end of year?
questions.solution:
P’s total investment = 50000 × 4 + (50000 – 20000) × 8 = 440000

Q’s total investment = 40000 × 6 + (40000 + 70000) × 6 = 900000

Ratio of their profit = ratio of their investments = 440000 ∶ 900000 = 22 ∶ 45

Sum of ratios = 22 + 45 = 67

P’s share = (22/67) × Total profit = 11000

∴ Total profit = 11000 × (67/22) = Rs. 33500

questions.question: The average weight of 25 candles is 40 grams. If some candles of weight 50 grams each were removed then the average weight becomes 37.5 grams. How many candles of weight 50 grams each were removed?
questions.solution:
Weight of 25 candles = 25 × 40 = 1000 grams

Let ‘x’ candles of 50 grams each were removed

Weight of remaining (25 – x) candles = (25 – x) × 37.5

⇒ 1000 – 50x = (25 – x) × 37.5

⇒ 1000 – 50x = 937.5 – 37.5x

⇒ 50x – 37.5x = 1000 – 937.5

⇒ 12.5x = 62.5

⇒ x = 62.5/12.5 = 5

∴ 5 candles of 50 grams each were removed.

questions.question: Simple interest on a sum for 9 months at 8% per annum is Rs. 270. What is the value (in Rs) of the sum?
questions.solution:
Let the sum be Rs. P

Simple interest = (Principal × Rate × Time) /100

⇒ 270 = (P × 8 × 9/12) /100

⇒ P = (270 × 12 × 100) / (8 × 9) = Rs. 4500

∴ The sum is Rs. 4500

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price is Rs. 575. If profit percentage is 23%, then what is the selling price (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
∵ Cost price + Profit = Selling price

⇒ Profit = Selling price – Cost price = Rs. 575

⇒ 23% of Cost price = 575

⇒ Cost price = 575/0.23 = Rs. 2500

∴ Selling price = 2500 + 575 = Rs. 3075

questions.question: A merchant marks the price of his articles 20% above the cost price. If he allows 20% discount, then what is the profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the cost price be Rs. ‘x’

Marked price = (100 + 20)% of x = 1.2x

Discount price = 20% of Marked price = 0.2 × 1.2x = 0.24x

Selling price = Marked price – Discount price = 1.2x – 0.24x = 0.96x

∵ Selling price is less than the cost price, there is a loss

Loss % = [(x – 0.96x)/x] × 100 = 4%

∴ There is a loss of 4%

questions.question: What is that least digit that must be added to the product 5786 × 5784 to make it a perfect square?
questions.solution:
Let the number to be added by ‘x’

In order to make a perfect square of 5785, we can write,

⇒ (5785)² = 5786 × 5784 + x

⇒ (5785)² = (5785 + 1) × (5785 – 1) + x

⇒ (5785)² = (5785)² – 1 + x [∵ (a + b)(a – b) = a² – b²]

⇒ x = 1

∴ The least number to added is 1

questions.question: 20 boys do one fourth of a work in 25 days. How many more boys will be required to complete the remaining work in 50 days?
questions.solution:
20 boys’ 25 days’ work = 1/4

⇒ 20 boys’ 1 day work = 1/4 × 1/25 = 1/100

⇒ 1 boy 1 day work = 1/20 × 1/100 = 1/2000

⇒ 1 boy 50 days’ work = 50 × 1/2000 = 1/40

⇒ Remaining work = 1 – 1/4 = 3/4

⇒ No. of boys required to do remaining work in 50 days = (3/4) / (1/40) = 30

∴ No. of more boys required = 30 – 20 = 10

questions.question: When Gopal walks from A to B and returns from B to A on a cycle, it takes him 46 minutes. When walking both ways, it takes him 75 minutes. If he rides the cycle both ways then what will be the total time (in minutes) taken by him?
questions.solution:
Time taken in walking from both sides = 75 min.

Time taken in walking from one side = 75/2 = 37.5 min.

Time taken in walking from one side + cycling from one side = 46 min

Time taken in cycling from one side = 46 – 37.5 = 8.5 min.

∴ Time taken in cycling from both sides = 2(8.5) = 17 min.

questions.question: The lengths of the two diagonals of a rhombus are 8 cm and 15 cm respectively. Find its area (in cm²).
questions.solution:
Area of rhombus = 1/2 × product of diagonals

∴ Area of given rhombus = (8 × 15)/2 = 60 cm²

questions.question: Find the area (in cm²) of a semi-circle of radius 35 cm.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius = 35 cm

**Formula used:**

Area of semi-circle with radius ‘r’ = πr2/2

**Calculation:**

Area of given semi-circle = (22/7) × (35 × 35)/2 = 1925 cm2

**∴ Area of given semi-circle is 1925 cm²**

questions.question: Find the total surface area (in cm²) of a right circular cone of diameter 14 cm and slant height 10 cm.
questions.solution:
For a right circular cone with radius of ‘r’ units and slant height of ‘l’ units,

Total surface area = πr(l + r)

Radius of given cone = 14/2 = 7 cm 

∴ Total surface area = (22/7) × 7 × (10 + 7) = 374 cm²

questions.question: ΔDEF is right angled at E. If m∠D = 45°, then find the value of (tanF + 1/3).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

ΔDEF is right angled traingle. 

∠D = 45°

**Concept used:**

Sum of angles of a triangle = 180°

**Calculation:**

⇒ ∠D + ∠E + ∠F = 180°

⇒ 45° + 90° + ∠F = 180°

⇒ ∠F = 180° – 135° = 45°

(tan F + 1/3)

⇒ tan 45° + 1/3 

⇒ 1 + 1/3

⇒ 4/3

∴ The required value of (tan F + 1/3) is 4/3.

questions.question: In ΔXYZ measure of angle Y is 90°. If cosecX = 17/15, and XY = 4cm, then what is the length (in cm) of side YZ?
questions.solution:
In ∆XYZ shown below,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b888f434fa9fe899fbbde35291da7de5c3bc4ac4c0d02301f37002a5d63de35.png] 

cosec X = hypotenuse/opposite = XZ/YZ = 17/15

Let XZ be 17x and YZ be 15x

Given, XY = 4 cm

Using Pythagoras theorem,

XZ² = XY² + YZ²

⇒ (XY)² = (XZ)² - (YZ)2

⇒ (XY)2 = (17x)² - (15x)²

⇒ (XY)2 = 64x²

⇒ XY = 8x

⇒ 8x = 4

⇒ x = 1/2

⇒ YZ = 15 × 1/2

**∴ YZ is 7.5 cm**
